en.headline: Customs seize 7kg of suspected cannabis at airport, arrest two mainland women
en.dek: Two women aged 50 and 54 arriving from Bangkok were each found with about 3.5 kilograms in their carry-on bags; the estimated value is HK$1.4 million.
body: Hong Kong Customs detected two drug trafficking cases at Hong Kong International Airport on Friday and seized about 7 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds with an estimated market value of HK$1.4 million, arresting two women.

The suspects, a 50-year-old and a 54-year-old mainland woman, both arrived from Bangkok, Thailand. During clearance, officers found about 3.5 kilograms of suspected cannabis buds in each woman’s carry-on baggage. The cases remain under investigation.

Customs said it would continue to step up enforcement based on intelligence analysis and risk management, focusing on passengers from high-risk areas. The department reminded the public not to take part in drug trafficking for money and not to carry items for others without knowing their contents. Under the Dangerous Drugs Ordinance, trafficking carries a maximum penalty of a HK$5 million fine and life imprisonment.

zh.headline: 海關機場檢約7公斤懷疑大麻花 拘兩名內地女子
zh.dek: 兩名分別50歲及54歲、從曼谷抵港的女子手提行李各藏約3.5公斤，市值估計約140萬元。
body: 香港海關周五在香港國際機場偵破兩宗入境旅客販毒案件，共檢獲約7公斤懷疑大麻花，估計市值約140萬元，並拘捕兩名女子。
兩名被捕人分別為50歲及54歲內地女旅客，均從泰國曼谷飛抵本港。海關人員清關時，在她們的手提行李內分別發現約3.5公斤懷疑大麻花。案件仍在調查中。
海關表示會繼續根據情報分析及風險管理原則，重點檢查來自高風險地區的旅客，加強打擊販運毒品。當局呼籲市民切勿貪圖金錢利益參與販毒，亦勿在未確定物品屬性下協助他人運送。根據《危險藥物條例》，販運危險藥物最高可被判罰款500萬元及終身監禁。
